records.title: Shopaholic
records.identity: NCPC 2007 PDF identifies Problem H as Shopaholic; Kattis archive index independently maps Shopaholic to slug shopaholic
records.observed: Lindsay shops during buy-three-pay-two promotions where the cheapest item among each group of three is free. She may split purchases across multiple counter visits to maximize the total discount.
records.excerpt: Lindsay is a shopaholic. Whenever there is a discount of the kind where you can buy three items and only pay for two
records.inputOutput: Input: test cases, item count and item prices. Output: maximum discount achievable by selecting which items to present together at each counter visit.
records.scenarioNotes: Concrete retail story and non-obvious batching decision, but still a short sorting/greedy task. Not approved as a long scenario.

records.title: Phone List
records.identity: NCPC 2007 PDF identifies Problem A as Phone List; Nordic 2007 archive also lists Phone List with slug phonelist
records.observed: A phone catalogue is inconsistent if one phone number is a prefix of another, illustrated by an emergency number intercepting a longer caller's number.
records.excerpt: Given a list of phone numbers, determine if it is consistent in the sense that no number is the prefix of another.
records.inputOutput: Input: test cases and lists of unique phone numbers. Output YES if no number is a prefix of another, otherwise NO.
records.constraints: 1 ≤ t ≤ 40; 1 ≤ n ≤ 10,000; each phone number has at most 10 digits.
records.scenarioNotes: A concrete telecom catalogue failure scenario, but extremely compact trie/prefix-check problem. Not approved as a long scenario.
